column1: # Written by Claude (origin "claude"). One line per entry:  entry id|typical learner mistake|usage note
# Notes are in English. Either text column may be empty.
cs:být:verb|In the past tense the auxiliary jsem, jsi … is used in the first and second person only: "byl jsem", "byl jsi", but "byl" (he was).|
cs:vy:pronoun||Vy is the plural "you" and also the polite form (vykání), with the verb in the second person plural: "Jak se máte?"
cs:ty:pronoun||Ty (tykání) is for friends, family and children; with strangers use vy.
cs:se:pronoun||Se is the reflexive pronoun and goes in the second position of the clause: "Jmenuji se Petr".
cs:mít:verb||"Mít rád" means to like: "mám rád kávu". Mít + infinitive means to be supposed to: "mám jít".
cs:jít:verb|Jít is going on foot; going by vehicle is jet. For repeated movement use chodit and jezdit.|
cs:jet:verb|Jet is going by vehicle; on foot it is jít.|
cs:ahoj:interjection||Ahoj is hi and bye among friends. Formal: dobrý den and na shledanou.
cs:prosím:interjection||Prosím means please, you're welcome and pardon?
cs:moci:verb|Moci is being able or allowed; for a learned skill use umět: "umím plavat" (I can swim).|
cs:umět:verb|Umět is for learned skills, including languages: "umím česky".|
